attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The 'best guess' hedge in the post applies to the sentence before this one. This sentence is a firm statement about the present, and the proposition keeps the coding-uses concession.

contract.note: The plain reading (useful applications alongside recurrent material errors) is ordinary. Reading 'inherently' as a characteristic current weakness rather than an immutable limit is a mild, flagged choice. It fits the speaker's 'from the start, not solved' context.

evidence.note: 2025 developer survey reports practical coding uses. These are self-reported perceptions, but enough to show some practical uses exist.
Multinational 2025 evaluation of four assistants found significant issues in 45% of news responses, described as systemic. This is recurrent material error across common systems.
RCT found experienced developers were slowed down despite believing AI helped. This tempers claims of coding gains but does not refute that some practical uses exist.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's 2025 reading, both parts are met. Some coding uses are attested (e1, self-reported), and an independent evaluation across several commonly used assistants shows systemic, material error rates (e2). Nothing in the packet shows dependable performance without verification. The evidence covers mainly the news domain, and the stronger 'immutable' sense of the claim is untested.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: An existence-level causal claim limited to 'some people'. The proposition matches the statement.

contract.note: Treating contributory causation as enough, and hospitalized psychosis as serious, is an ordinary reading. Requiring clinical rather than media evidence is fair and demanding.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed UCSF case report, published Dec 2025, before the post. Clinicians reviewed the chatlogs, found the chatbot reinforced the patient's delusions, and documented hospitalization. Confounders (stimulants, sleep loss, mood history) are acknowledged.

reviews.rationale: The clinical case report shows a material contributing role for a chatbot in serious, hospitalized psychosis before Feb 2026. That meets the contract's existence-level support condition, and the contract does not require sole causation. Confounders limit how much of the cause can be pinned on the chatbot, but they do not show coincidence. The support rests on one documented case.

attribution.note: Marcus asserts 'Turns out it wasn't' in his own voice, endorsing Ovide's reporting. The claim is his.

semantics.note: A denial that generative AI contributed about half of US GDP growth. The period and measure are not stated in the source.

contract.note: Reading the denial as 'materially below half' is fair. The first-half-2025 period is provisional, and the original statement's measure was never verified. The result turns on gross versus import-adjusted accounting, which the speaker did not specify.

evidence.note: Tech investment net of imports was about 20% of growth over 9 months, and Evercore's first-half figure is similar. Without netting imports, the AI boom's share is put at 70%. The measure chosen decides the answer, and these are broad tech categories.
AI-related categories were 39% of growth through Q3 2025. That is a different period, and the categories are broader than generative AI.
Methodology note saying there is no consensus on how to identify AI in national accounts. It is not outcome evidence.

reviews.rationale: The packet cannot verify the original November statement's period or measure, or the Ovide article. Import-adjusted estimates put broad tech below half, but the gross figure cited for the first half is 70%. No source isolates generative AI. With the measure undetermined and the contract's source requirements unmet, the evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: A three-part causal claim stated in emphatic, figurative language. The proposition keeps all three parts.

contract.note: Reading 'ripping apart' as widespread, substantial damage and 'flooding the zone' as large-scale production is ordinary. Requiring all three parts follows from the conjunction.

evidence.note: A 2023 Turkish school experiment found unrestricted GPT access harmed later unaided learning, and safeguards mitigated the harm. It is local and shows a mechanism, not system-wide damage.
Shows systemic news-answer errors across assistants. This partly supports the information-ecosystem part, but it does not measure ecosystem-wide damage.
Estimates about 3M sexualized Grok images in 11 days, showing scale. Consent was not assessed, and the definition includes swimwear.
Canadian privacy regulator found xAI/X did not verify consent for sexualized deepfakes in the Jan 2026 incident. Supports the nonconsensual part.
2023 Harvard RCT found a well-designed AI tutor improved learning. It is local and does not refute harm elsewhere.

reviews.rationale: The deepfake part is substantially supported: e3 shows large scale and e4 shows the regulator's consent finding. The information part has partial support from e2. Nothing representative shows system-wide educational damage, and e1 and e5 are local and conflicting. No part is contradicted, but the conjunction cannot be confirmed, so the claim is unresolved.
